title: Benchmark Report Social Posts Pack (LinkedIn + X) — Latency per Dollar
content:
Redwood Inference — Social Copy Pack
Project: Public Benchmark Report (Production Economics: latency per $)
Owner: Ben Carter (w/ Soojin + Renee + Tyler)
Last updated: 2025-02-18

-----------------------------
0) Notes / guardrails (please read)
-----------------------------
Audience split:
- LinkedIn: broader engineering leadership, product, procurement-adjacent; keep it crisp, credible, avoid hype.
- X: engineers/ML folks; more detail is OK; thread format works best.

Claims + language guardrails (align with external claims guidelines):
- Don’t say “fastest” / “best” / “#1” unless Legal + Methodology sponsor explicitly signs off for that exact claim.
- Always anchor to: workload definition + region + model version + time window.
- Use: “We measured…”, “In our benchmark…”, “Under this workload…”, “Results vary; see methodology.”
- Avoid competitor callouts in social unless explicitly approved.

Must-include links in most posts:
- Landing page (report + interactive tables)
- Methodology appendix (or “Methodology” anchor on landing)

Assets to attach (preferred):
- 1 hero chart image (latency/$ overview by model family)
- 1 region table screenshot (NA/EU/APAC)
- 1 methodology diagram (workload + measurement window)
Alt text reminder for LinkedIn images.

-----------------------------
1) Canonical link targets (placeholders until final URLs are live)
-----------------------------
Primary landing page:
- https://redwoodinference.com/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar/

Methodology appendix (if separate):
- https://redwoodinference.com/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar/methodology/

Blog launch post (if used):

“Reproduce a smaller-scale version” example (docs/examples):

-----------------------------
2) UTM plan (Tyler Benson — marketing ops)
-----------------------------
Campaign naming (consistent across channels):
- utm_campaign=benchmark_latency_per_dollar_2025q1

Default UTMs by channel:
- LinkedIn company page:
  utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=benchmark_latency_per_dollar_2025q1
- LinkedIn employee posts (optional but recommended):
  utm_source=linkedin_employee&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=benchmark_latency_per_dollar_2025q1
- X (company):
  utm_source=x&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=benchmark_latency_per_dollar_2025q1
- Partner posts (if provided links):
  utm_source=partner&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=benchmark_latency_per_dollar_2025q1&utm_content={partner_slug}

utm_content conventions (to map copy variants):
- Format: {platform}_{angle}_{variant}_{asset}
- Examples:
  - utm_content=li_launch_v1_hero
  - utm_content=li_methodology_v2_diagram
  - utm_content=x_thread_v1_none
  - utm_content=x_region_apac_v1_table

utm_term (optional):
- Use for paid only. Leave blank for organic.

Short links:
- Prefer full link for transparency on LinkedIn.
- For X, OK to use a short link ONLY if it preserves UTMs (e.g., branded shortener). If using a shortener, confirm it does not strip query params.

Example final URL (LinkedIn launch v1):
https://redwoodinference.com/benchmarks/latency-per-dollar/?utm_source=linkedin&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=benchmark_latency_per_dollar_2025q1&utm_content=li_launch_v1_hero

-----------------------------
4) LinkedIn — Company page posts
-----------------------------

4.1 Launch announcement (LONG) — LI_LAUNCH_V1
Angle: New benchmark report + credibility + CTA
Asset: hero chart

Copy:
We just published our latest benchmark report on production economics: latency per dollar for popular open models, broken down by cloud region.

Why we did this:
Teams aren’t choosing models in a vacuum anymore—they’re choosing *serving outcomes*: latency, throughput, cost, and reliability, in the regions they actually run.

What’s inside:
• Results by model family and region (NA/EU + an APAC region)
• A clear methodology (workloads, concurrency, warmup/caching policy)
• Notes on variance and how to interpret results responsibly

If you’re building LLM features in production (or trying to justify inference spend), this is meant to be a practical reference.

Download the report + view tables: {LINK_WITH_UTM}
Methodology: {METHODOLOGY_LINK_WITH_UTM}

(As always: results vary by workload—methodology details and constraints are included.)

Suggested UTM:
- utm_content=li_launch_v1_hero

Alt text (for hero chart):
“Bar chart comparing latency per dollar across multiple model families, shown separately for each cloud region.”


4.2 Launch announcement (SHORT) — LI_LAUNCH_V2
Angle: quick CTA, minimal text
Asset: hero chart

Copy:

Report + tables: {LINK_WITH_UTM}

4.3 “Production economics” framing (LONG) — LI_ECON_V1
Angle: explain the metric + why it matters to engineers + procurement
Asset: none (or simple text graphic)

Copy:
“Which model is best?” is increasingly the wrong first question.

In production, you care about *what you can deliver per dollar* while staying inside latency and reliability targets.

That’s why our benchmark report focuses on production economics—latency per dollar (with supporting throughput + cost metrics), broken down by region.

If you’re:
• migrating from a prototype to production,
• planning dedicated capacity,
• or trying to compare options across regions,
this should save time.

Read the report: {LINK_WITH_UTM}
How we measured: {METHODOLOGY_LINK_WITH_UTM}

Suggested UTM:
- utm_content=li_econ_v1_none


4.4 Methodology credibility (LONG) — LI_METHOD_V1
Angle: reproducibility + constraints + no hype
Asset: methodology diagram

Copy:
Benchmarks are only useful if you can understand (and challenge) the methodology.

In our latency-per-dollar report we:
• define the workload (chat + embeddings baseline)
• specify concurrency/sequence length distributions
• use explicit warmup + caching policies
• report variance + rerun rules where applicable
• publish constraints so teams can interpret results responsibly

If you’ve been burned by cherry-picked numbers, start with the methodology section:
{METHODOLOGY_LINK_WITH_UTM}

Then explore results by region/model:
{LINK_WITH_UTM}

Suggested UTM:
- utm_content=li_method_v1_diagram

Alt text (methodology diagram):
“Diagram showing benchmark workload inputs, concurrency, warmup phase, measurement window, and derived metrics including latency per dollar.”


4.5 Region spotlight (EU / data residency) — LI_REGION_EU_V1
Angle: EU performance + data residency + Dedicated/Private CTA (soft)
Asset: region table screenshot (EU highlighted)

Copy:
For teams with EU users (or strict data residency requirements), region-by-region performance isn’t a nice-to-have—it changes the economics.

Our benchmark report breaks out latency per dollar by region (including EU), with the exact workload definition and measurement details.

Explore the EU tables + methodology here:
{LINK_WITH_UTM}

If you need dedicated or private deployments in-region, the report also outlines how to think about capacity and reliability tradeoffs.

Suggested UTM:
- utm_content=li_region_eu_v1_table

Alt text:
“Table showing benchmark metrics by model for the EU region, including latency percentiles, throughput, and derived latency per dollar.”


4.6 Region spotlight (APAC) — LI_REGION_APAC_V1
Angle: APAC coverage + routing/fallback mention
Asset: region table screenshot (APAC highlighted)

Copy:
APAC users deserve first-class performance too.

Our benchmark report includes an APAC region breakout so teams can compare production economics region-by-region—not just overall averages.

Report + tables: {LINK_WITH_UTM}
Methodology: {METHODOLOGY_LINK_WITH_UTM}

Tip: If you’re serving multiple geos, pay attention to routing policies and fallback behavior—small differences can dominate end-user latency.

Suggested UTM:
- utm_content=li_region_apac_v1_table


4.7 “How to use this report” (practical) — LI_HOWTO_V1
Angle: guidance + reduces skepticism
Asset: none

Copy:
How we recommend using the latency-per-dollar benchmark report:
1) Find your closest workload match (chat vs embeddings baseline).
2) Filter by the regions you actually deploy in.
3) Treat results as directional unless your token distribution and concurrency are similar.
4) Use the methodology section to sanity-check assumptions (warmup, caching, measurement window).
5) If you’re making a decision, run a small reproduction against your own prompt set.

Report: {LINK_WITH_UTM}
Methodology: {METHODOLOGY_LINK_WITH_UTM}

Suggested UTM:
- utm_content=li_howto_v1_none

-----------------------------
7) X (Twitter) — Thread options
-----------------------------

7.1 Technical thread (7 tweets) — X_THREAD_TECH_V1
Goal: earn trust w/ engineers; drive to methodology + tables.

1/
We just published a benchmark report on production economics: latency per dollar (plus throughput + cost metrics) for popular open models, by cloud region.
{LINK_WITH_UTM}

2/
Why latency/$? In production you don’t just want “cheap tokens” or “fast p50”. You want *what you can deliver per dollar* while meeting latency + reliability targets.

3/
We define the workload (chat + embeddings baseline), the concurrency/sequence length distributions, and the measurement windows. No mystery settings.

4/
We also call out variance + rerun rules. If the numbers move a lot run-to-run, that’s a result too (and you should treat it accordingly).

5/
Region matters. The same model can look very different across NA/EU/APAC depending on hardware pools, routing, and real-world network paths.

6/
If you’re making a decision, use this report as a starting point—then reproduce a smaller-scale version with your own prompt set.
(Methodology + reproduction notes are linked in the report.)

7/
Report + tables: {LINK_WITH_UTM}
Methodology: {METHODOLOGY_LINK_WITH_UTM}

Suggested UTM:
- utm_content=x_thread_tech_v1_none


7.2 “How to read the report” thread (5 tweets) — X_THREAD_HOWTO_V1
1/
How to use our latency-per-$ benchmark report without getting misled:

2/
Filter to your region(s). If you ship in EU, don’t optimize off US-only numbers.

3/
Match your workload shape: concurrency + token distribution dominate outcomes.

4/
Read methodology: warmup/caching policy and measurement window matter a lot.

5/
Then treat results as directional → reproduce on your prompt set if it’s a purchasing decision.
